newsitem.title: HAITI: U.S. observers call Haiti poll "lost opportunity".
newsitem.headline: U.S. observers call Haiti poll "lost opportunity".

text.p: A U.S. observer team said on Monday senate and local elections in Haiti, which drew far fewer voters than expected, were a "lost opportunity" to boost democracy on the impoverished island.

The low turn-out for Sunday's polls indicated a great deal of frustration among the electorate, Utah Lt. Gov. Olene Walker, leader of the International Republican Institute delegation, told a news briefing.

"Such sentiments, which appear to be widespread, are not encouraging for Haiti's democratic development," Walker said. "The weak turn-out severely undermines the process begun in 1990 and now places an even greater responsibility on Haiti's government and all the nation's leaders to overcome yesterday's lost opportunity."
The election was a significant step toward bringing democratic rule to a grassroots level in Haiti, which has spent much of its history under dictatorship.
"These high stakes appear to have been ill-defined by the nation's political leaders," Walker said.

The civic education programme was late and half-hearted, the IRI report said. Observers had seen election workers tampering with ballot sheets and there had been a "significant breakdown in the collection process," it said.
Problems arose with voter registration, with some people unable to find out where they should cast ballots. On the bright side, there was no major violence.

Georges Fauriol, Americas director at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, said it was clear people were frustrated at the failure of President Rene Preval's governmemt to improve their lives but the low turnout indicated they were losing faith in opposition politicians as well.
